current_determination: R63 identifies the R62 loss-of-regulator-memory residue as a nonhyperbolic rigorous-RG stable-fiber/mixed-boundary theorem species. In normalized coordinates X_k=(x_k,K_k), x_k=g_k^{-2} is marginal and K_k denotes complementary complete-density coordinates. The linearized finite-horizon stable fiber delta x_k=H_k delta K_k satisfies H_N=0 and H_k=(a_k-H_{k+1}c_k)^{-1}(H_{k+1}A_k-b_k); the effective transverse multiplier is A_k+c_k H_k. Hence strict complementary contraction plus sufficiently controlled cross derivatives yields cross-cutoff loss of memory after marginal retuning. The key native fork is whether Balaban's local extraction makes the coupling recursion exactly triangular in (g,K), in which case b_k=0 and the theorem reduces largely to irrelevant difference contraction, or whether a nontrivial stable graph is required. Published absolute ultraviolet-stability bounds do not by logical form provide these derivative estimates. Dimock III 'Convergence' is convergence of the scalar phi^4_3 expansion leading to a stability bound, not cross-cutoff Yang-Mills state convergence. Bauerschmidt-Brydges-Slade supplies a rigorous control example showing that the mixed-boundary stable-manifold theorem species is standard but not automatically applicable to non-Abelian gauge theory.
